claims.text: Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 produced by vacuum-arc melting is a dual-phase refractory high-entropy alloy.
The untreated alloy has a relatively coarse and heterogeneous precipitate distribution within a fine-grained BCC matrix.
The proposed intervention is annealing at 900 °C for 5 minutes followed by water quenching.
The rapid thermal post-treatment will produce a refined, uniformly distributed population of nanoscale Mo-W-rich precipitates in a fine-grained BCC matrix.
In situ monitoring can be used to tune the treatment and avoid undesirable grain growth or incomplete homogenization.
Short high-temperature exposure followed by rapid quenching breaks up larger precipitate aggregates.
Short high-temperature exposure followed by rapid quenching promotes a homogeneous distribution of nanoprecipitates.
Refined Mo-W-rich nanoprecipitates act as nucleation sites for deformation twinning or TRIP-like transformations.
The proposed twinning or TRIP-like transformations delay strain localization.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the post-treated alloy will exhibit increased tensile ductility.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the post-treated alloy will deform more uniformly under quasi-static loading.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the post-treated alloy will deform more uniformly under dynamic loading.
The post-treated alloy will retain high compressive strength comparable to the untreated baseline.
The post-treated alloy will retain impact-induced energy release comparable to the untreated baseline.
The untreated vacuum-arc-melted baseline has coarser precipitates and less uniform microstructural features than the proposed post-treated alloy.
